title.narrative: Provision of nutritious food vouchers to support drought affected population in Omaheke, Kavango East and Kavango West regions.

description.narrative: The project will complement the efforts of the Government of the Republic of Namibia in addressing the impact of the ongoing drought in the country. The project aims to ensure that 64,996 people in IPC 4 in the three regions namely, Omaheke, Kavango East and Kavango West are provided with resources to access adequate and nutritious food. Given their vulnerability, the primary target group of this intervention will be households with pregnant and breastfeeding women as well as children under the age of 5. Their levels of malnutrition as well as proneness to deterioration of their current levels are the driving factors in prioritizing these groups. The programme envisages two modalities of transfer. The first targeted group (households with pregnant and breastfeeding women) will be provided with a commodity voucher to redeem their nutritious food items from locally contracted retailers. The provision of the monthly commodity vouchers (Maize Meal 20kg, Fortified Instant Porridge 4 kg, Tin Fish 1.6 kg and Vegetable Cooking Oil 750 ml) for 3 months will empower the households to have access to safe nutritious food, ensuring that their daily food and nutrition intake needs are met. Whilst this enhances nutrition intake, it contributes directly to the 1000 days approach as well as preventing negative coping mechanisms.The second group to be targeted will be children aged 6 months to 4 years who attend free early childhood centres that are supported by the Ministry of Gender, Equality, Poverty Eradication and Social Welfare, Government of Namibia. This second cohort will be provided with cooked safe, nutritious hot meals three times a week at those Centres for a total duration of 3 months. The Cooperating Partner will be provided with funds to procure the commodities for the meal preparations. WFP will provide standard menus and ensure proper training & monitoring through its cooperating partner and our own resources to ensure the nutritional quality, safety & hygiene of the cooked meals provided at the centres meets recommended requirements and standards.WFP will conduct retail capacity assessments to identify retailers that are geographically closer to the people we serve and have the capacity to meet specifications and stock the required food items. These retailers will further be encouraged to stock larger quantities to always ensure their availability to the people we serve. In collaboration with UNICEF, WFP will support the roll-out of adequate nutrition education and awareness campaigns targeting the local communities, to teach them the importance of consuming balanced diet using the four food groups. As a result, the targeted community will be encouraged to focus on making informed dietary choices, leading to improved nutrition status and overall health and well-being. Cross cutting issues such as accountability to affected people (AAP), protection from sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), gender based violence (GBV), community feedback mechanism (CFM) , will also be entwined in the various activities under this intervention. Details of these are provided in later sections.
